title: Capital Gains
outcomes: Identify capital assets, transfers and holding periods.
Compute capital gains including the indexation comparison.
Apply special provisions for depreciable assets, slump sales and firms.

meta.exam_tip: Classify the asset and holding period first; exemptions and rates follow from that.

concepts.title: Capital asset, transfer and period of holding
body: A capital asset under section 2(22) is property of any kind held by the assessee, plus securities held by FPIs and specified ULIPs, but excludes stock-in-trade, personal effects (other than jewellery, archaeological collections, drawings, paintings, sculptures and works of art), rural agricultural land, and specified gold bonds and deposit schemes.

Period of holding: listed securities, UTI units, equity-oriented fund units and zero coupon bonds are short-term if held for up to 12 months; other assets for up to 24 months. Holding periods of previous owners are included where the asset was acquired by gift, will, inheritance, amalgamation, demerger and similar modes.

Section 67 charges gains on transfer; section 70 lists transactions not regarded as transfer — e.g. distribution on partition of a HUF, gifts and wills, transfers between a holding company and its wholly-owned Indian subsidiary, amalgamations and demergers meeting conditions, conversion of companies into LLPs meeting conditions, reverse mortgages and conversion of gold into electronic gold receipts.
concepts.analogy: Identify the asset, then the holding period, then whether there was a transfer.
concepts.work: Listed shares held for 11 months give short-term gains.

concepts.title: Computation of capital gains
body: Section 72: capital gain = full value of consideration − expenditure on transfer − cost of acquisition − cost of improvement. Indexation is not allowed when computing income under this head.

For land or building acquired before 23 July 2024 by a resident individual or HUF, tax on the gain is the lower of 12.5% without indexation and 20% with indexation (the excess E = A − B is ignored). Indexed cost uses the CII of the transfer year (384 for 2026-27) over the CII of the first year held or 2001-02, whichever is later.

Section 90 deals with cost: FMV on 1 April 2001 (capped at stamp duty value for land and buildings) may be taken for assets acquired before that date; self-generated assets like goodwill and certain rights have nil cost unless purchased; bonus shares allotted after 1 April 2001 have nil cost. Stamp duty value is deemed consideration for land and buildings, subject to tolerance.
concepts.analogy: Sale price minus costs; old property gets a lower-of comparison.
concepts.work: Land bought in 2005-06 for ₹25 lakh and sold for ₹1.2 crore gives tax of about ₹7.59 lakh using indexation.

concepts.title: Special cases: depreciable assets, slump sale, firms
body: Depreciable assets (section 74): gains on transfer from a block are always short-term — where sale proceeds exceed opening WDV plus additions, or the block ceases to exist.

Slump sale (section 77): transfer of an undertaking for a lump sum without values for individual assets. Net worth is cost; FMV of the undertaking is deemed consideration; gains are short-term if the undertaking was held for 36 months or less, and a CA report is required.

Firms and partners: when a firm distributes a capital asset to a partner on reconstitution or dissolution, its FMV is the firm's consideration (section 67(10) and section 8); gains on excess payments to a retiring partner are taxed in the firm and attributed to remaining assets. Assets introduced by a partner as capital contribution are valued at the amount credited to his capital account.
concepts.analogy: Special rules override the general formula.
concepts.work: Selling a whole division for a single price is a slump sale.

concepts.title: Exemptions from capital gains
body: Section 82: LTCG on a residential house is exempt if invested in one house in India bought one year before or two years after, or built within three years; if gains do not exceed ₹2 crore, the assessee may once in a lifetime invest in two houses. The exemption is capped at ₹10 crore.

Section 85: LTCG on land or buildings invested within six months in long-term specified bonds is exempt up to ₹50 lakh across years. Section 86: LTCG on any other asset is exempt proportionately when net consideration is invested in a residential house (subject to owning no more than one other house), capped at ₹10 crore. Section 83 covers agricultural land replaced by agricultural land.
Amounts not invested before the return date must be deposited in the Capital Gains Accounts Scheme by the due date. Selling the new asset within three years withdraws the exemption.
concepts.analogy: Reinvest in the right asset, within the window, up to the cap.
concepts.work: A ₹3 crore gain reinvested ₹2.2 crore in a house and ₹50 lakh in bonds leaves ₹30 lakh taxable.

concepts.title: Rates of tax on capital gains
body: Section 196: STCG on STT-paid listed equity shares, equity-oriented fund units and business trust units is taxed at 20%. Other STCG is taxed at slab rates.

Section 198: LTCG on such equity shares (STT paid on acquisition and transfer, with notified exceptions) and fund/business trust units (STT on transfer) above ₹1,25,000 is taxed at 12.5%. Section 197: other LTCG at 12.5%, with the indexation comparison for old land and buildings.
Resident individuals and HUFs may adjust unexhausted basic exemption limit against such gains; Chapter VIII deductions cannot be set against them.
concepts.analogy: 20% for short-term listed equity; 12.5% for long-term above ₹1.25 lakh.
concepts.work: LTCG of ₹4 lakh on listed shares gives tax of ₹34,375 before cess.

illustrations.title: Land bought before 23 July 2024
illustrations.q: Nandini, a resident individual, bought a plot in F.Y. 2005-06 (CII 117) for ₹25,00,000 and sold it in T.Y. 2026-27 (CII 384) for ₹1,20,00,000. Her other income exceeds the basic exemption limit. Compute tax on the long-term capital gain (before cess).

illustrations.title: Reinvesting gains from a house
illustrations.q: Karan, a resident individual, earns LTCG of ₹3,00,00,000 on selling a residential house in August 2026. He buys one new house in India for ₹2,20,00,000 in January 2027 and invests ₹50,00,000 in long-term specified bonds within six months of the sale. Compute the taxable LTCG.

summary: Section 72 computation; old land indexation comparison.

viva.q: How is indexation used for land acquired before 23 July 2024?
viva.model: For resident individuals and HUFs, tax is the lower of 12.5% on unindexed gain and 20% on indexed gain, ignoring the excess.
Transfer of an undertaking for a lump sum consideration without assigning values to individual assets and liabilities.

viva.q: When can two houses be bought under section 82?
viva.model: When the long-term gain is up to ₹2 crore, at the assessee's option, once in a lifetime.

viva.q: What is the time limit for section 85 bonds?
viva.model: Six months from the date of transfer, with a limit of ₹50 lakh.

viva.q: Can Chapter VIII deductions be set against LTCG?
viva.model: Chapter VIII deductions are barred against such gains; only the unexhausted basic exemption limit of residents is adjustable.
